# YouTube\n\n取 YouTube 视频的信息、下载视频/音频、抓字幕:
# YouTube

Fetch YouTube video information, download video or audio, and extract subtitle text. Powered by [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp).

## What it does

- **Video information**: title, channel, duration, view count, description, available formats, and subtitle languages. No media download. Use this before deciding which video or format to download.
- **Video download**: returns a platform file reference that downstream workflow nodes can use. Select a resolution or a specific `format_id` returned by Video information.
- **Audio download**: fetches the audio track. Original audio is the default and avoids re-encoding. Selecting MP3, M4A, or Opus uses ffmpeg; the `transcoded` output indicates whether conversion occurred.
- **Subtitle text**: removes timestamps and duplicate lines, preferring manually supplied subtitles and using automatic captions when necessary. This is usually faster than downloading audio and transcribing it.

## Common workflows

| Goal | Workflow |
|---|---|
| Track channel topics | Scheduled trigger → Video information → Subtitle text → LLM summary → Knowledge base |
| Archive a video | Video download (1080p) → Object store |
| Extract the spoken content | Subtitle text; if unavailable, Audio download → Transcription |

## Resolution and transcoding

YouTube stores multiple video and audio streams for each video. Selecting a resolution chooses an existing stream; it does not create a resolution that the source does not provide.

| Processing | When it happens | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Merge / remux** | Video and audio are separate streams | Combines streams without re-encoding; `merged` reports this |
| **Transcode** | You select MP3, M4A, or Opus audio | Re-encodes with ffmpeg; takes additional time and can reduce quality; `transcoded` reports this |

Choose original audio to keep the source encoding. Choose MP3 when compatibility matters more than avoiding conversion.

## Limits and notes

- Defaults are **720p and 512 MB**. Set a limit to `0` to remove it. Container disk capacity and operation timeouts still apply. The plugin rejects downloads whose reported size exceeds the configured limit before downloading the media.
- Automatic captions can contain mistakes. Check quotations against the original audio; `automatic` identifies automatically generated subtitles.
- Downloads depend on regional availability and login requirements. Restricted videos may require cookies.
- Download only content you are authorized to process. Public availability does not grant permission to redistribute content.

## Latest channel releases

Enter a channel URL or `@handle`, such as `https://www.youtube.com/@YouTube` or `@YouTube`.
The default limit is 10, with a range of 1–50. Choose Videos, Shorts or Streams.
The operation reads only that channel tab, preserves its recent-release order, and neither downloads media nor scans the complete history. Community text posts are not included.

The `videos` array includes each item's `id`, `title`, `url`, duration, views, thumbnail, and any available upload date or live status. Channel lists may omit dates; `upload_date` stays empty in that case. Missing numeric metadata is 0, which does not establish an actual zero count. Pass an item's `url` to Get video information when full metadata is needed.

Monitoring example: scheduled trigger → Get latest channel releases → deduplicate video IDs against a data table → subtitles or download → save processed IDs. The workflow owns cross-run deduplication; the plugin does not store monitoring state. This operation uses the same optional cookies and proxy credential.

## Optional credentials

Create a YouTube credential from the plugin detail, then attach it to an access group or select it in a test call or workflow node.

- **Login cookies**: paste the complete Netscape `cookies.txt` contents, not a file path or an HTTP Cookie header. The secret input preserves line breaks and masks the saved value.
- **Proxy URL**: optionally enter a proxy reachable from the plugin process, such as `http://proxy.example.com:7897`. URLs containing a username and password are stored as secrets.

Both fields are optional; anonymous calls remain available. Each non-empty credential field overrides its corresponding environment variable. Blank fields fall back to `YTDLP_COOKIES` (a file path) or `YTDLP_PROXY`. Deployment defaults are shared by calls that do not override those fields.
Each extraction uses its own temporary cookie file and deletes it afterwards. Refreshed cookies are not written back to the platform credential.

Follow the [official cookie export guide](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#exporting-youtube-cookies). Keep cookies out of chat, logs and ordinary workflow inputs. Replace expired cookies in the credential without restarting the replica. If login verification persists, check the session and proxy exit; credentials do not guarantee that upstream restrictions disappear.

The health check validates cookie format, ffmpeg and proxy connectivity. Success does not verify the login session; test **Get video information** with your target video after saving.

## Official catalog and deployment

The official catalog reference is `sokel/youtube`. It provides video downloads, audio downloads, metadata, and subtitles. `youtube-transcript` is a separate plugin with a different operation contract.

Install this entry from the catalog, create an access group, then start a replica using the catalog's pinned image and that group's token:

```bash
docker run -d --restart unless-stopped \
  -e SOKEL_ENDPOINT=https://sokel.example.com \
  -e SOKEL_TOKEN=skp_xxx \
  ghcr.io/sokel-dev/sokel-plugin-youtube:0.3.0
```

Prefer platform credentials for cookies and proxy settings. Existing environment variables remain supported. `YTDLP_COOKIES` must point to a writable file because yt-dlp saves cookies. If mounting a read-only secret, first copy it to a temporary file with mode `0600` at startup and point the variable to that copy.
